_comment: The environment-variable name template and .env value quoting (Phase 23,
step 1), asserted from both src/ts/state.ts (envName / quoteEnvValue /
unquoteEnvValue) and envv-cli/src/envfile.rs (env_name / quote_env_value /
unquote_env_value).
This fixture exists because there were three name builders before it and
they disagreed: dotenvKey (provider + key_id) fed the .env and YAML
exports, envKey in import-export.ts (provider only) fed the k8s and tfvars
exports, and data::env_key in the CLI (provider only) fed all four of its.
The same entry exported under two different names depending on which button
you pressed, and nothing anywhere said so.
The template is:
[PREFIX_] PROVIDER [_KEYID] [_VERSION] [_LABEL] [_ROLE]
KEYID is a deliberate deviation from the Phase 23 design's six segments —
see the header comment in src/ts/state.ts for why.
`quoting` asserts the round trip, not the bytes: parse(write(v)) == v is
the property that matters, and `written` is pinned alongside it only so a
change to the escaping shows up as a diff rather than passing silently.

names.why: the plain case
a role turns the bare name into a role-tagged one
role `value` is the absent role, not a segment
key_id keeps the place it has held since Phase 3
a bare version number gains its V
and a v-prefixed one does not double it
a dotted version keeps both halves
a dated version is a version
a word-shaped version keeps its first letter — `beta`, not `ETA`
a v-word is not a version number either
the label sits after the version
a hyphenated label collapses to one underscore
a provider with a space
runs of punctuation collapse and the edges are trimmed — never SPOTIFY__ID
a provider starting with a digit is not a legal identifier without help
an empty role adds no segment
the consumer prefix is opt-in
and is absent when it is not opted into
only the first prefix is used
lower case is offered, not assumed
preserve keeps what was typed, still normalising illegal characters
a cookie's __Host- prefix is stripped, not transliterated
and so is __Secure-
an entry with nothing usable still generates a legal name
a missing provider is UNKNOWN, as it has always been

roles.why: no primary_role keeps the bare name — every deployed .env depends on this
the reported bug: a client id must not export as though it were the key
the worked example from the request, end to end
an issuer whose second half is not called a secret
primary_role `value` is the absent role, not a VALUE segment
an empty secret_role falls back to SECRET rather than vanishing

_comment: E9: the reference grammar and the name template occupy the same
syntactic position. `${SPOTIFY_V2}` can mean provider SPOTIFY with
key_id V2 (the legacy split) or the SPOTIFY entry whose version is 2
(the template). Where both exist and disagree the reference is refused
rather than silently answered — a wrong value written into a config is
the Phase 21 defect class.
Each case names an entry by its `provider` field; `expect` is the
`account_name` of the entry that must be found, or null for refused.

cases.why: an exact provider still wins before anything else
the legacy Provider_keyid split still resolves
the template resolves a version nobody could address before
two honest answers is refused, not guessed
a name matching nothing is still nothing

quoting.why: a plain token is written bare
so are the characters a URL, a path and a fingerprint need
a trailing space would otherwise be eaten by the parser's trim
a comment character would otherwise truncate the value
a single quote needs no escaping inside double quotes
a dollar would otherwise be substituted by the shell
a newline is escaped rather than emitted — the parser's backslash continuation must never see one
a cookie jar is the shape that motivated this
and a User-Agent is the other one
the empty string quotes to "" — a bare KEY= is how unset is spelled

unquoting.why: single quotes are literal, as every shell and dotenv library treats them
one stray quote is not a quoted value
